title: Domain F Authoring Specification — Section F Technology & Analytics

quantity.description: Consolidate 110 archived Section F clone items into 37 unique replacement items (1 per clone group). Each replacement item replaces ~3 template-rotated clones.
39 retained seeds (19 Pack C + 20 Pack D) — full CAQS §1.6 certification pipeline.

topics: IT general controls and application controls
Business continuity planning and disaster recovery
topicMix.coverageTarget: Even distribution across all 10 topic areas. No single topic should exceed 15% of total items. Pack B Section F topic distribution serves as the target distribution.

blueprintTargets.losMapping: Each item must map to a specific LOS in the IMA CMA Part 1 Content Specification Outline — Section F (Technology & Analytics)
blueprintTargets.losPrecision: LOSTag must be CSO-precise (e.g., 'F.1.b Data governance frameworks') not generic ('F. Technology & Analytics')
blueprintTargets.verification: Blueprint Review gate confirms LOSTag against current IMA CSO before Certification Candidate status

difficultyTargets.antiInflation: Definition-recall items (e.g., 'What is blockchain?') = Easy. Single-step application (e.g., identify appropriate IT control) = Moderate. Multi-step analysis (e.g., evaluate cybersecurity risk scenario) = Difficult.

requiredElements: Framework or principle citation (COSO IT, COBIT, NIST, ISO 27001, etc.)
Why the correct answer is correct with substantive reasoning
Common exam trap or misconception identified and countered

perDistractor.requirement: Choice-specific. Explains WHY this specific choice is wrong. References the specific concept, framework, or misconception that would lead a learner to select this distractor.

explanationWrong.dl008Compliance: EW[CorrectChoice] must be empty string — verified at Technical Review gate.

distractors.plausibility: Must represent genuine practitioner errors or misconceptions in Technology & Analytics
distractors.specificity: Must be topic-specific — no generic 'none of the above' or obviously wrong choices
distractors.misconceptionBasis: Derived from common IT audit findings, cybersecurity incident patterns, or technology implementation failures

stem.clarity: Unambiguous. Contains all technical data needed. No undefined acronyms.
stem.completeness: All values and scenario details explicitly stated.
stem.fairness: Tests Technology & Analytics knowledge, not obscure IT terminology or vendor-specific knowledge

metadata.productionStatus: Draft → Technical Review → Blueprint Review → QA Review → Certification Candidate

instructionalStandards.applicationFocus: Items should teach Technology & Analytics concepts through practical business scenarios, not just definition recall. Each item should simulate a real-world finance/IT professional decision.
instructionalStandards.scenarioBased: Where applicable, present mini-case scenarios: 'A company is implementing a new ERP system. The CFO asks about IT general controls. Which control...'
instructionalStandards.distractorQuality: Distractors should reflect common practitioner mistakes — e.g., confusing IT general controls with application controls, misunderstanding data governance roles, mixing up cybersecurity frameworks.
instructionalStandards.realism: Business context must be realistic for a CMA candidate — manufacturing, service, healthcare, financial services organizations of varying sizes.

benchmark.reason: 100% certified. Gold standard for Section F. All items have substantive EC (400+ chars), choice-specific EW, precise LOSTags, and realistic business scenarios.

governanceCompliance.dl013: No template boilerplate in any field
governanceCompliance.caqs16: Six-dimension verification: Correctness, Precision, Difficulty Calibration, Distractor Engineering, Blueprint Alignment, CMA Part 1 Relevance
